You are a professional biblical lexicographer fluent in Spanish. Translate the following English lexicon entry into Spanish.

Lemma: H3637

ENGLISH GLOSSES TO TRANSLATE:
  Terse gloss: "To be ashamed, be disgraced (Nifal); to humiliate, put to shame (Hifil); to be caused shame (Hofal)"
  Readable gloss: "A verb whose three stems map a full circuit of shame: the Nifal expresses being ashamed, the Hifil the causative act of humiliating another, and the rare Hofal the passive experience of having disgrace inflicted. When Moses asks about Miriam, 'Would she not be ashamed seven days?' (Num 12:14), the Nifal captures disgrace felt inwardly. Boaz orders his men not to 'humiliate' Ruth (Ruth 2:15) -- the Hifil targets dignity. Arabic cognate 'kalama' (to wound) hints at the physical origin behind the psychological sense."

SENSES:
  Sense 1: "be ashamed, be disgraced (Nifal)"
    Enriched: The Nifal stem: experiencing shame or public disgrace as an internal state. Numbers 12:14 sets the paradigm -- shame that lasts and isolates. In Isaiah 45:16-17 idolaters 'are ashamed' while Israel 'shall not be ashamed,' framing shame as salvation's antithesis. Ezra 9:6 turns shame inward as penitence. Spanish 'avergonzarse' reflects the passive-reflexive Nifal.
    Existing Spanish translations: avergonzarte, fueron-humillados, fui-humillado, los-avergonzados, muy-avergonzados, se-avergonzaren, se-avergonzaron, sean-humillados, sería-avergonzada, te-humilles, y-confundíos, y-humillados, y-humillarse, y-se-avergüencen, y-sean-confundidos, y-sean-humillados, y-te-avergonzarás, y-te-avergüences
  Sense 2: "put to shame, humiliate (Hifil)"
    Enriched: The Hifil stem: actively causing shame to another person. Judges 18:7 describes a city with no one to 'put them to shame'; Ruth 2:15 instructs reapers not to 'humiliate' the gleaner; 1 Samuel 20:34 records Jonathan's anger because Saul had 'disgraced' David. Spanish 'avergonzar' (transitive) and French 'humilier' mark the causative agent.
    Existing Spanish translations: avergonzará, cuando-avergüence, la-avergüencen, lo-avergonzó, los-avergonzamos, me-habéis-avergonzado;, quien-avergonzara, quien-te-avergüence?, sonrojarse, y-nos-humillaste
  Sense 3: "be humiliated by another (Hofal)"
    Enriched: The Hofal stem (passive of Hifil): being caused shame by an external agent. Only three occurrences distinguish this from the Nifal by emphasizing that disgrace was inflicted. In 1 Samuel 25:15, servants report they 'were not shamed' by David's men; Jeremiah 14:3 depicts nobles 'put to shame' by drought. The construction stresses the agent behind the humiliation.
    Existing Spanish translations: fuimos-avergonzados, y-se-humillaron, y-serás-humillada
